text:
maria: heads up — we've had 3 customers this morning get a generated invoice instead of a refund. billing queue shows the autorouter picked generate_invoice_v2 for requests that were clearly refund intents.
noah: can you paste a minimal repro payload and a router log? helps narrow whether it's schema collision or signature aliasing.
maria: minimal repro attached here — reproduced from support UI -> API proxy
```json
POST /v1/handle
{
  \"customer_id\": \"C-91234\",
  \"amount\": 120.00,
  \"intent\": \"refund\",
  \"currency\": \"USD\",
  \"notes\": \"refund for order 9987\"
}
```
maria: router log snippet:
```
[2024-07-03T09:42:10Z] trace=tr_9a8b selected_tool=generate_invoice_v2 confidence=0.61 matched_fields=[amount,currency,notes]
[2024-07-03T09:42:10Z] trace=tr_9a8b resolved_sig=invoice.create_v2 schema_required=[amount,currency,memo]
[2024-07-03T09:42:10Z] trace=tr_9a8b invoked-> /tools/generate_invoice_v2 args={\"amount\":120.00,\"currency\":\"USD\"}
```
ivan: interesting — the payload didn't include an explicit operation/action key, so router used fuzzy match on amount/currency. invoice and refund signatures both accept numeric amount fields so tie-break favored invoice.
junior_support: customers reported API responded 200 with invoice id, but they expected refund. We got multiple tickets, one escalation to finance.
noah: quick root cause: our function-calling selector currently treats identical primitive field names as strong positive signal. if two tools share 'amount' + 'currency', we bias toward historically higher-usage tool. generate_invoice has higher prior, so it wins.
maria: repro trace ids: tr_9a8b, tr_9a9c, tr_9aaf — all same pattern.
noah: proposed hotfix options:
- require discriminator: add required enum property 'action_type' for refund vs invoice (breaks some callers)
- lower prior weight in selector for tools that share >2 identical required primitives
- prefer tools with explicit 'intent'/'operation' field in payload
- rollout a soft-check that rejects ambiguous selection and returns 409 with suggestion (safer short term)
ivan: can we do the soft-check quickly? return 409 + hint so UI/integrations fail fast rather than doing wrong side-effect.
maria: support prefers soft-check for now; finance wants automatic rollbacks for affected invoices.
noah: implement soft-check in routing layer today — patch prepared, test run in staging.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued — canary patch routing/selector: reduce prior_weight for generate_invoice_v2 by 0.4; add ambiguity check -> return 409 with body {error: \"ambiguous_tool_choice\"} in canary region us-west-2.
ivan: monitoring: add alert for 409_ambiguous_tool_choice spike and also track rollbackable-invoices metric.
junior_support: created ticket SUP-812 and attached impacted trace ids and customer emails; set P2->P1 because finance is involved.
maria: thanks. after canary we should also add library docs recommending callers pass explicit operation/action enum. long-term: add model eval to detect ambiguous signature clusters.
noah: I'll own the runtime change. plan: canary in 30m, monitor 2 hours, then global if no regressions.
maria: noted — I'll update affected customers with temporary workaround (add \"action_type\":\"refund\"). :thumbsup:
